resources.string: The Kai conversation appears once the phone is paired with lmgw.
Looking up the folder \'%1$s\' on lmgw…
Local models are paused (GPU hold); %1$s answers for them
On lmgw\'s Devices card choose Pair a device…, then scan its QR code, tap its link on this phone, or paste the link here.
Scan it here, not with the system camera or Lens: their frame may leave the phone, and the code carries a pairing token.
The scanner needs the camera. Allow it, or paste the link instead.
Android didn\'t let Kai keep the microphone in the background. Open Kai and try again.
Kai needs the microphone for voice: allow it, or use the conversation by text.
Waiting for %1$s: a push-to-talk press still talks
Kai\'s audio is muted until its next reply
The thread\'s mode, as lmgw reports it
Speaker when no headset is connected
Earpiece when no headset is connected
The phone\'s hardware canceller where it reports one, else WebRTC\'s
Half duplex: software echo cancelling, and speech does not interrupt Kai (tap the ring to stop it)
Kai interrupts itself on speaker: try software echo cancelling, or half duplex if that is not enough. A change applies from the next call.
Half duplex only: how long after Kai\'s speech ends the microphone still counts as its echo, in milliseconds; empty = lmgw\'s own value
Saved; a change applies from the next call.
Every number field needs a whole number (push-to-talk\'s tail and the echo tail may be empty: not set).
From the trigger to lmgw\'s first word on the call (the session, or its prompt), in seconds
Seconds of quiet before a call ends; 0 = never. A pending prompt counts as quiet.
How often Kai\'s playout is reported to lmgw while it speaks, in milliseconds; keep it well below lmgw\'s realtime.ping_interval_s

How long the microphone stays on after a push-to-talk release, in milliseconds; empty = not set, no tail. It must fit inside lmgw\'s webrtc_commit_window_ms (120 ms unless changed on lmgw): a longer tail needs that window raised, or the turn\'s last syllable is lost.
Another app holds the audio (a phone call?), so voice did not start. Try again once it is done.
Half duplex: Kai does not hear you while it speaks; tap the ring to stop it.
Kai was interrupted and is listening
Kai is waiting: hold to talk
Kai is waiting while another person\'s turn runs
Android refused to route the call to %1$s; its own choice stands.
Android did not switch the call to %1$s; its own choice stands.

resources.string: Approved: sent to lmgw, waiting for its answer.
Declined: sent to lmgw, waiting for its answer.
In this call: Kai speaks the answer once you decide.
Saying or typing something else declines it.
Unlock the phone to approve. Declining works while locked.
%1$s: not in the phone\'s secure hardware (TEE or StrongBox), so the key is only as safe as Android itself. Kai uses it all the same.
in secure hardware of an unknown kind
at a security level the phone does not say
The phone deletes its key and its pairing with this lmgw and stops holding its feed. Delete the device on lmgw\'s Devices card too.
A connect (the whole URL race), an answer\'s head, the feed\'s first byte, in seconds
The wait before the race tries the next URL, in milliseconds
The feed\'s backoff ceiling while the app is visible, in seconds
The feed\'s backoff ceiling while the app is not visible, in seconds
The keep-alive the held feed asks of lmgw, in seconds; a silent drop is noticed after two
How often the phone asks again while it waits for the owner\'s Confirm, in seconds
The Chat folder the Kai conversation lives in
While the phone sleeps (Doze), Android may defer the retries and the dead-link check to a maintenance window.
Every field but the folder needs a whole number.
The system\'s dynamic colours instead of Kai\'s
Kai holds its connection to lmgw in the background, so replies and approvals reach the phone while the app is closed.
Notifications: without them Kai still runs, but no reply or approval shows.
Android asks once; if it was refused, allow it in Kai\'s app settings.
Battery: exempt Kai from battery optimisation, so Android keeps its connection.
On Samsung: Settings → Battery → Background usage limits → Never sleeping apps → + → Kai.
Kai is on the Never sleeping apps list
Kai is set up to run in the background.
Finish setup: Kai in the background
Kai needs the microphone for voice. Open Kai to allow it.
Android did not let the sheet open Kai. The call goes on here; open Kai from the launcher.
Closing this before your first words ends the call.
Closing this leaves the call going on in the background.
Closing this leaves the voice where it is.

As the digital assistant, Kai opens over whatever you are doing when you press and hold the side button (or the power button, or use the corner swipe), and listens at once. Closing it before your first words ends the call; after them the call goes on in the background. While Kai is the assistant, apps that use the system\'s speech recogniser get none from it (keyboards with a recogniser of their own are not affected).
Set Kai as the digital assistant app.
This phone does not offer the digital assistant to apps: the Quick Settings tile and the launcher shortcut start a call instead.
The side button: Settings → Advanced features → Side button → Press and hold → Kai (instead of the power-off menu).

The power button: where Settings offers it (System → Gestures → Press and hold power button → Digital assistant), choose it. Otherwise set it once from a computer with adb: adb shell settings put global power_button_long_press 5
The power button: Settings → System → Gestures → Press and hold power button → Digital assistant.
The power button\'s or the gesture\'s setting for the digital assistant, where the phone offers one; the corner swipe or the home button\'s long press open Kai too once it is the digital assistant.
On this phone the power button\'s long press is set to %1$d; the assistant\'s value is %2$d.
Android does not let Kai read the power button\'s long press setting, so it cannot say what it is set to.
The power button\'s long press is at the build\'s default (on LineageOS the power menu).
Microphone: allow it now, so an invocation listens at once instead of asking.
Kai is set up as your digital assistant.
Without the role, the Quick Settings tile \"Talk to Kai\" and the launcher shortcut \"Talk\" start a call too.
